title: Properties: stored, computed, observed and lazy

videos.script: A property is a name inside a type. This lesson is about what that name can hide. {{stored}} First the plain kind, a stored property. You will see a let property refuse to change, even inside a var. {{computed}} Then a property that stores nothing. A week's total, computed from its sessions every time it is read. It cannot fall out of step. {{observers}} Then code that runs around a change. Will set, before the new value lands. Did set, after it. You will watch one keep the minutes under six hundred. {{lazy}} A lazy property, built on the first read and never again. And the reason a struct only allows it through a var. {{static}} Properties of the type itself, one value for every instance. {{init}} And the initialiser, whose one job the compiler checks on every path. Including the one that refuses to build a session from bad input.
